subproblems.title: A proper injective C¹ chart with injective Dψ(v) makes N flat at ψ(v) along range Dψ(v)
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ and N ⊆ ℝ^P. Let V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on V and injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N, and such that V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. This is a local representation of N in the sense of Simon Ch. 2, 4.1, except that Dψ is only required to be injective at the point v. Let v ∈ V be such that Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v is injective. Then N is flat at ψ(v) along the range of Dψ(v): for every real ε > 0 there is a real ρ > 0 such that every z ∈ N with |z − ψ(v)| < ρ admits some h ∈ ℝ^d with |z − ψ(v) − Dψ(v)h| ≤ ε|z − ψ(v)|. All norms and distances are Euclidean.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ v) → v ∈ V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ∀ z ∈ N, dist z (ψ v) < ρ → ∃ h : Euclid d, ‖z - ψ v - fderiv ℝ ψ v h‖ ≤ ε * ‖z - ψ v‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (flatness of N at x) of the parent-supplied proof of approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace, specialized to one chart. The chart data that IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N supplies at x = ψ(v) are hypotheses here, and only injectivity of Dψ at v is used. The parent's phrase 'β → v as z → x (properness and injectivity)' is written out as a positive-minimum argument on a compact set. Book: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §4, 4.1–4.3 (local book/chapter-02.txt lines 849–871). There, properness makes a local representation a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ N, and Dψ has maximal rank.
Notation: |·| is the Euclidean norm and dist(a, b) = |a − b|. B(a, s) is the open ball and B̄(a, s) the closed ball. L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v is a continuous linear map ℝ^d → ℝ^P.
1. Setup. V is open and v ∈ V, so V is a neighbourhood of v. ψ is C¹ on V, hence differentiable on V (the order 1 is ≠ 0), hence Fréchet differentiable at v with derivative L. In Lean: (hψ.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (hV.mem_nhds hv), then .hasFDerivAt. ψ is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Since ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N, we have ψ(v) ∈ W.
2. Coercivity. L is injective and ℝ^d is finite-dimensional, so there is K > 0 with |h| ≤ K|Lh| for every h ∈ ℝ^d. If d = 0, every h is 0 and K = 1 works. Otherwise L is a linear bijection of ℝ^d onto the finite-dimensional subspace L(ℝ^d). Its inverse is a linear map between finite-dimensional normed spaces, hence bounded, and any K > 0 bounding it works. In Lean: LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, applied to (L : Euclid d →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) with LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr of the injectivity, gives K > 0 such that L is K-antilipschitz. ContinuousLinearMap.bound_of_antilipschitz then gives |h| ≤ K|Lh|.
3. First-order estimate. Put η := min(1/(2K), ε/(2K)) > 0. Then ηK ≤ 1/2 and η·(2K) ≤ ε. Because L is the derivative of ψ at v, ψ(β) − ψ(v) − L(β − v) = o(|β − v|) as β → v. Hence there is σ > 0 such that |ψ(β) − ψ(v) − L(β − v)| ≤ η|β − v| for every β ∈ ℝ^d with |β − v| < σ. In Lean: HasFDerivAt.isLittleO, then IsLittleO.def with constant η, then Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.
4. A compact set away from v. W is open and ψ(v) ∈ W, so there is δ₁ > 0 with B(ψ(v), δ₁) ⊆ W. Put δ₀ := δ₁/2 > 0. Then B̄(ψ(v), δ₀) ⊆ B(ψ(v), δ₁) ⊆ W, and B̄(ψ(v), δ₀) is compact, being closed and bounded in ℝ^P. By the properness hypothesis, A := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄(ψ(v), δ₀)) is compact. Hence C := A ∖ B(v, σ) is compact, as a compact set minus an open set. Note that C ⊆ V.
5. Positive separation on C. We show there is m > 0 with |ψ(β) − ψ(v)| ≥ m for all β ∈ C. If C = ∅, take m := 1. Otherwise the function β ↦ |ψ(β) − ψ(v)| is continuous on C, since C ⊆ V and ψ is continuous on V. So it attains its minimum on the nonempty compact set C at some β₀ ∈ C (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Put m := |ψ(β₀) − ψ(v)| ≥ 0. Suppose m = 0. Then ψ(β₀) = ψ(v) with β₀, v ∈ V, so β₀ = v by injectivity of ψ on V. But v ∈ B(v, σ) because σ > 0, whereas β₀ ∈ C lies outside B(v, σ). This contradiction shows m > 0.
6. Choice of ρ. Put ρ := min(δ₀, m) > 0, and let z ∈ N with |z − ψ(v)| < ρ. Then |z − ψ(v)| < δ₀, so z ∈ B̄(ψ(v), δ₀) ⊆ W, and hence z ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V). So z = ψ(β) for some β ∈ V, and β ∈ A because ψ(β) = z ∈ B̄(ψ(v), δ₀). Suppose |β − v| ≥ σ. Then β ∈ C, so by step 5 |z − ψ(v)| = |ψ(β) − ψ(v)| ≥ m ≥ ρ, contradicting |z − ψ(v)| < ρ. Hence |β − v| < σ.
7. The estimate. Take h := β − v. By step 3, |z − ψ(v) − Lh| = |ψ(β) − ψ(v) − L(β − v)| ≤ η|h|. Since Lh = (z − ψ(v)) − (z − ψ(v) − Lh), the triangle inequality gives |Lh| ≤ |z − ψ(v)| + η|h|. By step 2, |h| ≤ K|Lh| ≤ K|z − ψ(v)| + (ηK)|h| ≤ K|z − ψ(v)| + |h|/2. Hence |h| ≤ 2K|z − ψ(v)|. Therefore |z − ψ(v) − Lh| ≤ η|h| ≤ η·(2K)·|z − ψ(v)| ≤ ε|z − ψ(v)|.
8. Conclusion. For the given ε > 0, the number ρ > 0 has the required property. Every z ∈ N with dist(z, ψ(v)) < ρ admits h ∈ ℝ^d, namely h = β − v from step 6, with |z − ψ(v) − Dψ(v)h| ≤ ε|z − ψ(v)|. Step 2 covers the case d = 0, and step 5 covers the case C = ∅. This proves the statement.

theorem Submission.atsm_chart_image_flat : ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ v) → v ∈ V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ∀ z ∈ N, dist z (ψ v) < ρ → ∃ h : Euclid d, ‖z - ψ v - fderiv ℝ ψ v h‖ ≤ ε * ‖z - ψ v‖ := by
  intro P d N W V ψ v hV hW hψ hinj himg hprop hLinj hv ε hε
  set L := fderiv ℝ ψ v with hLdef
  have hdiff : DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ v :=
    (hψ.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (hV.mem_nhds hv)
  have hL : HasFDerivAt ψ L v := hdiff.hasFDerivAt
  have hcont : ContinuousOn ψ V := hψ.continuousOn
  have hψvW : ψ v ∈ W := by
    have : ψ v ∈ ψ '' V := mem_image_of_mem ψ hv
    rw [himg] at this
    exact this.1
  -- coercivity of the injective derivative
  obtain ⟨K, hKpos, hK⟩ := LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith (L : Euclid d →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)
    (LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr hLinj)
  have hcoer : ∀ h : Euclid d, ‖h‖ ≤ K * ‖L h‖ := fun h =>
    ContinuousLinearMap.bound_of_antilipschitz L hK h
  have hK0 : (0 : ℝ) < K := by exact_mod_cast hKpos
  set η : ℝ := min (1 / (2 * K)) (ε / (2 * K)) with hηdef
  have hη : 0 < η := lt_min (by positivity) (by positivity)
  have hηK : η * K ≤ 1 / 2 := by
    calc η * K ≤ 1 / (2 * K) * K := by gcongr; exact min_le_left _ _
      _ = 1 / 2 := by field_simp
  have hηε : η * (2 * K) ≤ ε := by
    calc η * (2 * K) ≤ ε / (2 * K) * (2 * K) := by gcongr; exact min_le_right _ _
      _ = ε := by field_simp
  -- first-order expansion
  obtain ⟨σ, hσ, hσball⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.1 (hL.isLittleO.def hη)
  -- a compact set away from v
  obtain ⟨δ₁, hδ₁, hδ₁W⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.1 hW (ψ v) hψvW
  set δ₀ : ℝ := δ₁ / 2 with hδ₀def
  have hδ₀ : 0 < δ₀ := by positivity
  have hcbW : closedBall (ψ v) δ₀ ⊆ W := (closedBall_subset_ball (by linarith)).trans hδ₁W
  have hA : IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' closedBall (ψ v) δ₀) := hprop _ hcbW (isCompact_closedBall _ _)
  set C := (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' closedBall (ψ v) δ₀) \ ball v σ with hCdef
  have hC : IsCompact C := hA.diff isOpen_ball
  have hCV : C ⊆ V := fun β hβ => hβ.1.1
  -- positive separation on C
  obtain ⟨m, hm, hmC⟩ : ∃ m : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ ∀ β ∈ C, m ≤ ‖ψ β - ψ v‖ := by
    rcases C.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hCe | hCne
    · refine ⟨1, one_pos, fun β hβ => ?_⟩
      rw [hCe] at hβ
      exact hβ.elim
    · have hfc : ContinuousOn (fun β => ‖ψ β - ψ v‖) C :=
        ((hcont.mono hCV).sub continuousOn_const).norm
      obtain ⟨β₀, hβ₀C, hβ₀min⟩ := hC.exists_isMinOn hCne hfc
      refine ⟨‖ψ β₀ - ψ v‖, ?_, fun β hβ => (isMinOn_iff.mp hβ₀min) β hβ⟩
      rcases (norm_nonneg (ψ β₀ - ψ v)).lt_or_eq with hlt | heq
      · exact hlt
      · exfalso
        have h0 : ψ β₀ = ψ v := by
          have h' := heq.symm
          rwa [norm_eq_zero, sub_eq_zero] at h'
        have hβv := hinj (hCV hβ₀C) hv h0
        apply hβ₀C.2
        rw [hβv]
        exact mem_ball_self hσ
  refine ⟨min δ₀ m, lt_min hδ₀ hm, ?_⟩
  intro z hzN hzd
  have hzcb : z ∈ closedBall (ψ v) δ₀ := mem_closedBall.2 (hzd.trans_le (min_le_left _ _)).le
  have hzim : z ∈ ψ '' V := by
    rw [himg]
    exact ⟨hcbW hzcb, hzN⟩
  obtain ⟨β, hβV, rfl⟩ := hzim
  have hβA : β ∈ V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' closedBall (ψ v) δ₀ := ⟨hβV, hzcb⟩
  have hβσ : dist β v < σ := by
    by_contra hcon
    have hβC : β ∈ C := ⟨hβA, fun hb => hcon (mem_ball.1 hb)⟩
    have h1 := hmC β hβC
    rw [← dist_eq_norm] at h1
    have h2 : min δ₀ m ≤ dist (ψ β) (ψ v) := (min_le_right _ _).trans h1
    linarith
  refine ⟨β - v, ?_⟩
  have hest : ‖ψ β - ψ v - L (β - v)‖ ≤ η * ‖β - v‖ := hσball hβσ
  have hLh : ‖L (β - v)‖ ≤ ‖ψ β - ψ v‖ + η * ‖β - v‖ := by
    calc ‖L (β - v)‖ = ‖(ψ β - ψ v) - (ψ β - ψ v - L (β - v))‖ := by congr 1; abel

  have hh : ‖β - v‖ ≤ 2 * K * ‖ψ β - ψ v‖ := by

        _ ≤ K * (‖ψ β - ψ v‖ + η * ‖β - v‖) := by gcongr
        _ = K * ‖ψ β - ψ v‖ + (η * K) * ‖β - v‖ := by ring
    have h3 : (η * K) * ‖β - v‖ ≤ 1 / 2 * ‖β - v‖ := by gcongr
    linarith
  calc ‖ψ β - ψ v - L (β - v)‖ ≤ η * ‖β - v‖ := hest
    _ ≤ η * (2 * K * ‖ψ β - ψ v‖) := by gcongr
    _ = (η * (2 * K)) * ‖ψ β - ψ v‖ := by ring

proof_key_steps: ψ is differentiable at v with injective derivative L = Dψ(v). Finite-dimensionality gives K > 0 with |h| ≤ K|Lh|. The first-order expansion gives σ > 0 with |ψ(β) − ψ(v) − L(β − v)| ≤ η|β − v| on B(v, σ), where η = min(1/(2K), ε/(2K)).

Properness, continuity and injectivity of ψ on V give m > 0 with |ψ(β) − ψ(v)| ≥ m on the compact set (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄(ψ(v), δ₀))) ∖ B(v, σ). Hence every z ∈ N with |z − ψ(v)| < min(δ₀, m) equals ψ(β) for some β ∈ V with |β − v| < σ.
With h = β − v, coercivity absorbs the remainder: |h| ≤ 2K|z − ψ(v)|. Hence |z − ψ(v) − Lh| ≤ η|h| ≤ ε|z − ψ(v)|.

subproblems.title: An approximate tangent plane of M lies in every subspace along which a set carrying H^n-almost all of M is flat
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and M, N ⊆ ℝ^P with H^n(M ∖ N) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] is the normalized n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure. No measurability of M or N is assumed. Let x ∈ ℝ^P, and let Q, T be linear subspaces of ℝ^P. Suppose N is flat at x along T: for every real ε > 0 there is a real ρ > 0 such that every z ∈ N with |z − x| < ρ admits some t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|. Suppose Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q). That is, finrank Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 (along 𝓝[>] 0), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). Then Q ⊆ T, i.e. Q ≤ T as submodules. Norms and distances are Euclidean.

Source: steps 3–6 of the parent-supplied proof of approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace. The flatness established in its step 2 is now a hypothesis, T is an arbitrary linear subspace, and x need not lie in N. Book: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 and Remark 1.5(1) (local book/chapter-03.txt lines 77–86). The resulting inclusion T_xM ⊆ T_xN is used in Ch. 4, 2.6–2.7 (book/chapter-04.txt lines 175–209).
Notation: H^n := μHE[n]. η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x), which is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r y. |·| is the Euclidean norm. B(a, s) and B̄(a, s) are the open and closed balls. dist(q, T) := inf over t ∈ T of |q − t| (Metric.infDist q T).
1. Set-up for contradiction. Let q ∈ Q; we show q ∈ T. Suppose q ∉ T. T is a finite-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and it is nonempty since 0 ∈ T. Therefore δ := dist(q, T) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos).
2. Test function. Let g(y) := max(0, δ/2 − |y − q|).
- g is continuous and g ≥ 0.
- If g(y) ≠ 0 then |y − q| < δ/2; otherwise δ/2 − |y − q| ≤ 0 and g(y) = 0. Conversely, |y − q| < δ/2 implies g(y) > 0.
- Hence g vanishes outside the compact ball B̄(q, δ/2), so g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).
- So g defines f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), the CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ⟨⟨g, continuity⟩, compact support⟩, with f(y) = g(y) for all y.
The parent normalizes |q| = 1 and uses ε = δ/8 and r < ρ/2. Here no normalization is made and the constants of step 4 are used instead; the mathematics is the same.
3. ∫_Q g dH^n > 0. By hypothesis finrank Q = n.
(a) The measure H^n⌞Q is regular (SimonGMT Chapter03 regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), in particular finite on compact sets. So the continuous, compactly supported g is H^n⌞Q-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
(b) The support of the measure H^n⌞Q is exactly Q (SimonGMT support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule). Since q ∈ Q and B(q, δ/2) is a neighbourhood of q, (H^n⌞Q)(B(q, δ/2)) > 0 (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall, whose explicit argument is the point q).
(c) B(q, δ/2) ⊆ {g ≠ 0}, so (H^n⌞Q)({g ≠ 0}) > 0. Since g ≥ 0 is integrable, ∫_Q g dH^n > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg).
4. Constants. |q| + δ > 0. Put ε := δ/(2(|q| + δ)) > 0, so that ε(|q| + δ) = δ/2. Let ρ > 0 be given by the flatness hypothesis for this ε: every z ∈ N with |z − x| < ρ admits t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|.
5. Vanishing of the blow-up integrals. Fix r with 0 < r < ρ/(|q| + δ). We show ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n = 0.
(a) H^n(η_r(M ∖ N)) = 0.
- η_r(M ∖ N) = r⁻¹·A, where A := {y − x : y ∈ M ∖ N} (Set.image_smul, Set.image_image).
- The translation y ↦ y − x is an isometry (dist_sub_right), so H^n(A) = H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- Since r⁻¹ ≠ 0, H^n(r⁻¹·A) = |r⁻¹|^n·H^n(A) = 0 (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
(b) {g ≠ 0} ∩ η_r(M) ⊆ η_r(M ∖ N). Let y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M and g(y) ≠ 0; it suffices to show z ∉ N. Suppose z ∈ N.
- By step 2, |y − q| < δ/2, so |y| ≤ |y − q| + |q| < |q| + δ/2.
- Since r ≠ 0, z − x = r·y. Hence |z − x| = r|y| ≤ r(|q| + δ) < ρ.
- By step 4 there is t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|.
- Then r⁻¹t ∈ T and y − r⁻¹t = r⁻¹(z − x − t). So |y − r⁻¹t| ≤ r⁻¹ε|z − x| = ε|y| ≤ ε(|q| + δ) = δ/2.
- Consequently δ = dist(q, T) ≤ |q − r⁻¹t| ≤ |q − y| + |y − r⁻¹t| < δ/2 + δ/2 = δ (infDist_le_dist_of_mem), a contradiction.
(c) {g ≠ 0} is open because g is continuous, hence Borel.
- By Measure.restrict_apply, which needs measurability only of {g ≠ 0} and not of η_r(M): (H^n⌞η_r(M))({g ≠ 0}) = H^n({g ≠ 0} ∩ η_r(M)).
- By (b) and (a), this is ≤ H^n(η_r(M ∖ N)) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
- So g = 0 almost everywhere for H^n⌞η_r(M) (ae_iff), and ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
6. Conclusion.
- Apply the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q to f: the function r ↦ ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n tends to ∫_Q g dH^n along 𝓝[>] 0.
- The interval (0, ρ/(|q| + δ)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). So by step 5 this function is eventually 0 along 𝓝[>] 0, and therefore also tends to 0 (Tendsto.congr').
- Since 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ, limits are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique). Hence ∫_Q g dH^n = 0, contradicting step 3.
- Therefore q ∈ T. As q ∈ Q was arbitrary, Q ≤ T.

open scoped CompactlySupported Pointwise in
theorem Submission.atsm_approxTangent_le_of_flat : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (N M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), μHE[n] (M \ N) = 0 → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ∀ z ∈ N, dist z x < ρ → ∃ t ∈ T, ‖z - x - t‖ ≤ ε * ‖z - x‖) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → Q ≤ T := by
  intro P n N M x Q T hnull hflat hQ q hq
  by_contra hqT
  have hTc : IsClosed (T : Set (Euclid P)) := T.closed_of_finiteDimensional
  have hδ : 0 < infDist q (T : Set (Euclid P)) :=
    (hTc.notMem_iff_infDist_pos ⟨0, T.zero_mem⟩).1 hqT
  set δ := infDist q (T : Set (Euclid P)) with hδdef
  -- the bump function
  set g : Euclid P → ℝ := fun y => max 0 (δ / 2 - ‖y - q‖) with hgdef
  have hgc : Continuous g :=
    continuous_const.max (continuous_const.sub (continuous_id.sub continuous_const).norm)
  have hg0 : 0 ≤ g := fun y => le_max_left _ _
  have hgsupp : ∀ y, g y ≠ 0 → ‖y - q‖ < δ / 2 := by
    intro y hy
    by_contra h
    have h' : δ / 2 ≤ ‖y - q‖ := not_lt.mp h
    apply hy
    exact max_eq_left (by linarith)
  have hgpos : ∀ y, ‖y - q‖ < δ / 2 → 0 < g y := fun y hy =>
    lt_max_of_lt_right (by linarith)
  have hgcs : HasCompactSupport g := by
    apply HasCompactSupport.intro (isCompact_closedBall q (δ / 2))
    intro y hy
    by_contra h
    apply hy
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm]
    exact (hgsupp y h).le
  let f : C_c(Euclid P, ℝ) := ⟨⟨g, hgc⟩, hgcs⟩
  have hf : ∀ y, f y = g y := fun y => rfl
  -- the plane integral is positive
  have hQn : Module.finrank ℝ Q = n := hQ.1
  have := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule hQn
  have hsupp := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule hQn
  have hint : Integrable g ((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict (Q : Set (Euclid P))) :=
    hgc.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hgcs
  have hpos : 0 < ∫ y in (Q : Set (Euclid P)), g y ∂μHE[n] := by
    rw [integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg hg0 hint]
    have hq' : q ∈ ((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict (Q : Set (Euclid P))).support := by
      rw [hsupp]
      exact hq
    have hball : 0 < ((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict (Q : Set (Euclid P)))
        (ball q (δ / 2)) :=
      (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall q).1 hq' _ (ball_mem_nhds q (by linarith))
    refine hball.trans_le (measure_mono ?_)
    intro y hy
    rw [mem_ball, dist_eq_norm] at hy
    exact (hgpos y hy).ne'
  -- constants
  have hqδ : 0 < ‖q‖ + δ := by positivity
  set ε : ℝ := δ / (2 * (‖q‖ + δ)) with hεdef
  have hε : 0 < ε := by positivity
  have hεq : ε * (‖q‖ + δ) = δ / 2 := by
    rw [hεdef]
    field_simp
  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ, hflatρ⟩ := hflat ε hε
  -- the blow-up integrals vanish for small r
  have hvan : ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < ρ / (‖q‖ + δ) →
      ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, f y ∂μHE[n] = 0 := by
    intro r hr hrρ
    have hnull' : μHE[n] (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' (M \ N)) = 0 := by
      have himg : Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' (M \ N) =
          r⁻¹ • ((fun y => y - x) '' (M \ N)) := by
        rw [← Set.image_smul, Set.image_image]
        rfl
      have hiso : Isometry (fun y : Euclid P => y - x) :=
        Isometry.of_dist_eq fun a b => dist_sub_right a b x
      rw [himg, Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ n (inv_ne_zero hr.ne'),
        hiso.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, hnull, smul_zero]
    have hsub : {y | g y ≠ 0} ∩ Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M ⊆
        Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' (M \ N) := by
      rintro y ⟨hgy, z, hzM, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨z, ⟨hzM, fun hzN => ?_⟩, rfl⟩
      have hyq : ‖Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z - q‖ < δ / 2 := hgsupp _ hgy
      set y := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z with hy
      have hy' : y = r⁻¹ • (z - x) := rfl
      have hzx : z - x = r • y := by
        rw [hy', smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul]
      have hynorm : ‖y‖ < ‖q‖ + δ / 2 := by
        calc ‖y‖ = ‖(y - q) + q‖ := by rw [sub_add_cancel]
          _ ≤ ‖y - q‖ + ‖q‖ := norm_add_le _ _
          _ < δ / 2 + ‖q‖ := by linarith
          _ = ‖q‖ + δ / 2 := by ring
      have hzxn : ‖z - x‖ = r * ‖y‖ := by
        rw [hzx, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg hr.le]
      have hdist : dist z x < ρ := by
        rw [dist_eq_norm, hzxn]
        calc r * ‖y‖ ≤ r * (‖q‖ + δ) := by gcongr; linarith
          _ < ρ / (‖q‖ + δ) * (‖q‖ + δ) := by gcongr
          _ = ρ := by field_simp
      obtain ⟨t, htT, ht⟩ := hflatρ z hzN hdist
      have hrt : r⁻¹ • t ∈ T := T.smul_mem _ htT
      have hyt : y - r⁻¹ • t = r⁻¹ • (z - x - t) := by
        rw [hy']
        exact (smul_sub _ _ _).symm
      have hyt' : ‖y - r⁻¹ • t‖ ≤ ε * ‖y‖ := by
        rw [hyt, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.2 hr.le)]
        calc r⁻¹ * ‖z - x - t‖ ≤ r⁻¹ * (ε * ‖z - x‖) := by gcongr
          _ = ε * ‖y‖ := by rw [hzxn]; field_simp
      have hle : δ ≤ ‖q - r⁻¹ • t‖ := by
        rw [← dist_eq_norm]
        exact infDist_le_dist_of_mem hrt
      have h2 : ε * ‖y‖ ≤ δ / 2 := by
        rw [← hεq]
        gcongr
        linarith
      have hlt : ‖q - r⁻¹ • t‖ < δ := by
        calc ‖q - r⁻¹ • t‖ = ‖(q - y) + (y - r⁻¹ • t)‖ := by congr 1; abel
          _ ≤ ‖q - y‖ + ‖y - r⁻¹ • t‖ := norm_add_le _ _
          _ < δ / 2 + δ / 2 := by
            have h1 : ‖q - y‖ < δ / 2 := by rw [norm_sub_rev]; exact hyq
            linarith
          _ = δ := by ring
      linarith
    have hopen : MeasurableSet {y | g y ≠ 0} :=
      (isOpen_ne_fun hgc continuous_const).measurableSet
    apply integral_eq_zero_of_ae
    rw [EventuallyEq, ae_iff]
    change (μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M)) {y | g y ≠ 0} = 0
    rw [Measure.restrict_apply hopen]
    exact measure_mono_null hsub hnull'
  -- conclusion
  have hlim := hQ.2 f
  have hev : (fun r : ℝ => ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, f y ∂μHE[n])
      =ᶠ[𝓝[>] 0] fun _ => 0 := by
    have hpos' : 0 < ρ / (‖q‖ + δ) := by positivity
    filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hpos'] with r hr
    exact hvan r hr.1 hr.2
  have hlim0 : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M,
      f y ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) :=
    tendsto_const_nhds.congr' hev.symm
  have heq := tendsto_nhds_unique hlim hlim0
  have hzero : ∫ y in (Q : Set (Euclid P)), g y ∂μHE[n] = 0 := heq
  linarith

proof_key_steps: If q ∈ Q ∖ T, then δ = dist(q, T) > 0 because T is closed. The bump g = max(0, δ/2 − |· − q|) lies in C_c and has ∫_Q g dH^n > 0, because spt(H^n⌞Q) = Q and H^n⌞Q is finite on compact sets (finrank Q = n).
The blow-up η_{x,r}(M ∖ N) is H^n-null: H^n is translation invariant and scales by |r⁻¹|^n.

Take ε = δ/(2(|q| + δ)) and 0 < r < ρ/(|q| + δ). Flatness of N at x along T makes g vanish on η_{x,r}(M ∩ N). So g = 0 H^n-a.e. on η_{x,r}(M) (restriction evaluated on the open set {g ≠ 0}), and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} g dH^n = 0.
The defining limit along 𝓝[>] 0 then forces ∫_Q g dH^n = 0, a contradiction. Hence Q ≤ T.
